title: Nasruddin's House is Too Small

full_text:
A poor peasant came to Nasruddin complaining: "Mulla, my house is a misery! I, my wife, our four children, and my mother-in-law live in a single tiny room. We are crowded, noisy, and at each other's throats. Help me!"

Nasruddin advised: "Bring your six chickens into the room to live with you."

The man was horrified, but trusted the Mulla. A week later, he returned weeping: "It is unbearable! Chickens are flapping in our faces!"

"Bring in your two goats," commanded Nasruddin. A week later: "Bring in your donkey and cow!"

The following week, the man returned in tears of madness: "I cannot live! The house is a roaring zoo of dung and noise!"

Nasruddin smiled calmly: "Now go home, take out the cow, take out the donkey, take out the goats, and take out the chickens!"

The man ran home, cleared the animals, and returned the next morning, beaming with joy: "Mulla, God bless you! Our house is so vast, quiet, and peaceful! We live in a royal palace!"
moral: True contentment is discovered by recognizing how much worse things could be.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Nasruddin's House is Too Small"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
